« La police a le droit de recourir à une: “Police are allowed to use deadly force as much as they want”
« Le gouvernement n’a pas proposé de sol: “The government hasn’t proposed solutions that can meet the needs of Black communities, including making sure they feel safe,” said Pierreson Vaval, director of the community organization Équipe RDP, at a press conference announcing the formation of a convoy against racial profiling.
On a récemment modifié les Guides des pr: Quebec’s and Montréal’s police practice guides were recently amended to include new recommendations.
Une première consultation publique de la: The Public Security Commission, which is responsible for examining issues related to the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM) and civil security, among other things, held a first public consultation earlier this week. But people affected by racial profiling feel that the responses from Montréal and Quebec City do not protect them from this kind of discriminatory behaviour and from brutality. In the Canadian city with the highest number of police officers per capita, many are proposing solutions to fix a situation that has gone on for years.
« La police a le droit de recourir à une: “Police are allowed to use deadly force as much as they want,” says Desmond Cole, a journalist and the author of The Skin We’re In: A Year of Black Resistance and Power. He points out that when someone is killed by police, it is most often a person who is Black, Indigenous or living with a mental health problem.
« La population reçoit le message que ce: “The public gets the message that these killings are necessary, that they’re deserved, or that the people who were shot were a threat to the community,” he notes. In his view, the normalization of this violence leads to police impunity.
« On sait d’avance qu’il n’y aura aucune: “We know in advance that there will be no consequences, that officers won’t be punished for using excessive force, because it’s their job to use that force,” he says, referring to the few convictions handed down in cases of police brutality or racial profiling. Mr. Cole believes that this approach, inherently tied to the very purpose of policing, cannot be reformed.
« La violence n’est pas la solution, et: “Violence is not the solution, and policing legally uses violence. We call the police to give them the ability to use it,” he says.
Desmond Cole dit être en faveur du défin: Desmond Cole says he supports defunding the police because, in his view, it is a measure that can lead to the abolition of police services. He explains his position: “You can’t reform a system of legalized violence, you have to replace it,” he maintains.
« La police constitue un gouvernement qu: “The police are a government that wields its violence against us [Black and Indigenous people], sometimes through the injustice of its policies, sometimes through their neglect. That’s what we need to focus on, rather than having an abstract conversation about how the police are funded,” he says.
Sur le plan des mesures, M. Cole croit q: In terms of measures, Mr. Cole believes that police officers should at the very least give up their firearms. “You don’t give certain people a bulletproof vest, a gun and a Taser so that they can negotiate with people,” the author illustrates.
Plusieurs sociétés ont des services de p: Many societies have police services that are not armed, including in the United Kingdom, on the African continent and in several Indigenous communities. This model has also been adopted by some police forces in Canada. In Ontario, for example, officers of the Nishnawbe-Aski Police Service (NAPS), the largest Indigenous police service in the country, are unarmed.
Depuis sa fondation il y a 26 ans, le NA: Since its founding 26 years ago, NAPS has not shot and killed anyone, and no officer has died on duty, despite a glaring shortage of resources. Mr. Cole argues that it’s not models we’re lacking, but will. “Who do the police open fire on here in Canada?” he asks. “Chantel Moore was shot during a so-called wellness check. Rodney Levi was killed. Deandre Campbell-Kelly called 911 for help; the police went into his home and shot him,” he says. Since it is Black and Indigenous communities that are affected, Mr. Cole suggests that solutions take into account what they have to say.
Il en va de même pour les personnes qui: The same goes for people living with mental health conditions, or who are under the influence of drugs or alcohol, who make up the vast majority of victims of police brutality. “You have to ask them,” he continues. “These people are certainly not going to say, ‘I’d like to be approached with a firearm.’ They’ll ask for support, for someone to listen, for crisis de-escalation services, to be taken to the hospital if they’re not feeling well.”
Pour résoudre les conflits, M. Cole sugg: To resolve conflicts, Mr. Cole suggests an approach that uses no violence at all, like the methods already used by social services, medical staff and education workers, among others. The author, who also works as a youth worker at a youth residential centre, says his job requires no weapons. “When I work at a residential centre, I work with young people who are constantly being stopped by the police.
Cette dernière vous dira que ces jeunes: The police will tell you that these kids use drugs and carry weapons, which is true for some of them. When they come to the centre and there’s a conflict, I’m not allowed to point a weapon at them. I have to learn to talk, to use my voice, to de-escalate the situation and to stand off to the side, which is less threatening. I have to be trained for that.”
M. Cole croit fortement que la communica: Mr. Cole strongly believes that communication and de-escalation should be part of the intervention methods used by the police and by the services that could replace them. “The mistake is asking why we don’t give police this training,” he says. “You also have to take their weapons away.”

Alain Babineau, conseiller en matière de: Alain Babineau, an adviser on racial profiling and discrimination at the Centre de recherche-action sur les relations raciales (CRARR), believes in reorganizing the police. He also believes the police can change the way they intervene. “There is clearly a lack of training when it comes to de-escalating situations or changing the way officers approach people,” he acknowledges.
Selon son expérience, le module qui trai: In his experience, the use-of-force module that all police officers in North America refer to covers how an officer should present themselves and use their voice.
« Malheureusement, la façon dont les pol: “Unfortunately, the way police communicate with people is often very aggressive and leads to confrontation. They act too quickly. There’s no reason for that if communication is done in a more humane way,” he explains.
<strong>Changer la police au lieu de la: Changing the police instead of defunding them
L’ancien officier de la GRC propose de r: The former RCMP officer proposes rethinking the role of the police in society. “I’m asking that we take duties away from police officers,” he says. He cites in particular non-criminal acts linked to issues such as mental health, homelessness, substance use or poverty. “You can’t criminalize any of these social problems,” he states. He proposes that these tasks no longer fall to police services and that the necessary budgets go toward the police’s core responsibilities, such as protection and prevention.
Alain Babineau s’oppose au définancement: Alain Babineau opposes defunding the police and wants the money being called for to be found elsewhere. “I suggest that the City look at all the services it offers to the public and reallocate the money to social services or mental health services,” he says. “Yes, it’s good to put money into social services, but what effect does that have in terms of client service?” he asks, before adding that 90% of the SPVM’s budget goes to employee salaries.
« La protection des communautés vulnérab: “The protection of vulnerable communities isn’t being analyzed,” he argues. If the police were defunded, Mr. Babineau thinks police training, social programs and community services would be affected. Mr. Babineau faults the provincial government and the municipal administration for not having held any consultations within communities. He levels the same criticism at the instigators of the movement calling for the police to be defunded.
La semaine dernière, plusieurs membres d: Last week, several members of Black communities in the Montréal and Lanaudière regions showed up at François Legault’s constituency office in L’Assomption. The “Black, proud and free behind the wheel” convoy handed in a document with 10 recommendations to end racial profiling. Among other things, it proposes adopting a law and regulations against racial profiling, institutionalizing police training on discrimination, racism and racial profiling, creating a database on the racial backgrounds of pedestrians and drivers who are stopped, and requiring officers to wear body cameras.
À Montréal, les femmes autochtones sont: In Montréal, Indigenous women are 18 times more likely to be stopped by police. “What are the police doing to remedy the problem?” asks Nakuset, director of the Native Women’s Shelter of Montréal, Nakustet Sohhisiwin. On May 3, the SPVM deployed 17 officers, the canine unit and 13 patrol cars to assist an Indigenous woman in psychological distress.
« C’était exagéré, les agents et les pas: “It was excessive, the officers and passersby were laughing at the situation, and the person was completely distraught,” she recalls. She deplores the city’s inaction on racial profiling, while the administration seems quick to react on other issues, such as replacing the statue of John A. Macdonald, which was recently vandalized.
Selon l’intervenante sociale, certaines: According to the social worker, some resources and solutions are already in the hands of the authorities, but they are not using them. She adds that police officers are not familiar with the Indigenous organizations to which they could refer people, or with the services of the Indigenous liaison officer, who can act as an interpreter. Ms. Sohhisiwin believes police services need better training.
Elle souhaite ainsi que la GRC soit form: She would like the RCMP to be trained by Indigenous police forces, the Peacekeepers. She also believes police forces should receive more training on violence against women, mental health and gender-based violence. In her view, social workers shouldn’t be counted on to support police during interventions, because they are already overwhelmed.
Mme Sohhisiwin suggère que les corps pol: Ms. Sohhisiwin suggests that police forces be modernized, even if that means dismantling them and replacing them with new cohorts. “Officers need sincere compassion and resources, and they must be required to work with the Peacekeepers,” she proposes.
« La SQ a été l’objet d’allégations d’ag: “The SQ was the subject of allegations of assaults against Indigenous women in Val-d’Or. No action was taken, and the women who spoke out were vilified,” she laments. The Viens Commission came out of those events, but since it tabled its report last September, the community is still waiting for action from police forces, Ms. Sohhisiwin observes.
« On y trouve des recommandations pour l: “There are recommendations in there for youth protection and for hospitals, but neither the police nor anyone else has implemented them. The norm is to ignore the problem completely.” Ms. Sohhisiwin suggests that everyone read the Viens Commission report and adopt best practices in order to improve relations with Indigenous people and people of colour.
